## Preambles
```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(brms)
```

- Install the `bcogsci` package
```{r}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("bnicenboim/bcogsci")
library(bcogsci)
```

## Exercise 1

- Load the dataset
```{r}
data("df_recall")
df_recall <- df_recall %>%
  mutate(c_set_size = set_size - mean(set_size))
# Set sizes in the data set:
df_recall$set_size %>%
  unique() %>% sort()
```

```{r}
# Trials by set size
df_recall %>%
  group_by(set_size) %>%
  count()

df_recall
```

- (Finally,) Fit the `fit_recall` model
```{r}
fit_recall <-
  brm(correct ~ 1 + c_set_size,
      data = df_recall,
      family = bernoulli(link = logit),
      prior = c(prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = Intercept),
                prior(normal(0, 0.1), class = b, coef = c_set_size)))
```
```{r}
posterior_summary(fit_recall,
                  variable = c("b_Intercept", "b_c_set_size"))

plot(fit_recall)
```
```{r}
# Average accuracy
alpha_samples <- as_draws_df(fit_recall)$b_Intercept
av_accuracy <- plogis(alpha_samples)
c(mean = mean(av_accuracy), quantile(av_accuracy, c(0.025, 0.975)))

# Decrease in accuracy
beta_samples <- as_draws_df(fit_recall)$b_c_set_size
odds_ratio <- exp(beta_samples)
c(mean = mean(odds_ratio),
  quantile(odds_ratio, c(0.025, 0.975)))
```

> The posterior mean odds ratio for centered set size was 0.835 (95% credible interval: [0.711, 0.977]), indicating that each additional item in the set was associated with approximately 16.5% lower odds of successful recall.

## Exercise 2

```{r}
mean(beta_samples < 0)
```

> Given the observed data and the model, there is a 98% posterior probability that increasing set size decreases the odds of successful recall.

## Exercise 3

```{r}
# Center the new set size using the original data mean
c_set_size_10 <- 10 - mean(df_recall$set_size)

# Predicted probability for each posterior draw
pred_10 <- plogis(alpha_samples + beta_samples * c_set_size_10)

# Posterior mean and 95% CrI
c(mean = mean(pred_10), quantile(pred_10, c(0.025, 0.975)))
```

> The posterior mean predicted recall accuracy at set size 10 is 72.3% (95% CrI: [53.3%, 88.1%]).
However, I have limited confidence in this prediction because set size 10 was never tested. The estimate assumes that the effect of increasing set size remains constant on log-odds scale. The relatively wide CrI (~35%p) also indicates increased uncertainty about the predicted accuracy.

## Exercise 4

> Since `fit_recall` is a logistic regression model fit that already assumed the belief that 
β ∼ Normal(0, 0.1), the refit would not make any change (apart from Monte Carlo variation).

> Just for sanity, I repeat the same code from Exercise 1 above and double-check:

```{r}
fit_recall <-
  brm(correct ~ 1 + c_set_size,
      data = df_recall,
      family = bernoulli(link = logit),
      prior = c(prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = Intercept),
                prior(normal(0, 0.1), class = b, coef = c_set_size)))

beta_samples <- as_draws_df(fit_recall)$b_c_set_size
odds_ratio <- exp(beta_samples)
c(mean = mean(odds_ratio),
  quantile(odds_ratio, c(0.025, 0.975)))
```
